meta.name: eMudhra Compromised Certificate and Go Runtime Audit

related.reason: A broader audit of Go runtime vulnerabilities would overlap but lacks the specific focus on certificate compromise.

meta.analysis: This is a hunt because a single detection rule cannot correlate a static trust anchor with the version of a specific runtime engine and the behavior of signed module loads. It requires pivoting between the trust store, software inventory, and execution telemetry.

scenario.summary: eMudhra mistakenly issued eight intermediate CA certificates with weak P-384 private keys that had as little as 3-8 bits of entropy, making them trivial for attackers to recover. Adversaries can leverage these recovered keys to perform Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) impersonation of web services or sign malicious software that appears legitimate to systems that have not yet updated their trust stores or Go runtime environments.

meta.rationale: Focus on developer workstations, build servers, and container hosts where Go runtimes and code signatures are most prevalent.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary impersonates a trusted service or signs a malicious binary using a compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate in an environment that lacks strict revocation checking or runs a vulnerable Go runtime.

hunt.name: eMudhra Compromised Certificate and Go Runtime Audit
hunt.description: This hunt identifies exposure to eight compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates whose private keys were generated with insufficient entropy. The hunt first finds hosts executing code signed by eMudhra. If it finds such activity, the hunt fans out to identify vulnerable Go runtimes (CVE-2026-111943) that ignore revocation and scans for certificate files matching known compromised fingerprints. An agent then weighs the combination of trust anchors and execution context to help an analyst decide on remediation.
